Advertisement Biopharma dealmaking remained active through the third quarter of 2026. DealForma data published by J.P. Morgan show 113 mergers and acquisitions worth $138.9 billion year to date, including 32 deals worth $31.1 billion in the third quarter.1 Two deals announced this week fall at different stages of that market. Teva acquired a late-stage neuroscience candidate, BXCL501, and an approved product from BioXcel Therapeutics through a bankruptcy court sale,2 while Rumi Therapeutics took an option on a compound from Enthorin Therapeutics that it describes as ready for an investigational new drug application.3 Teva’s deal includes contingent payments, while Rumi did not disclose financial terms.2,3Key FactsTeva: BioXcel neuroscience assets, incl. BXCL501Price: $57.5M upfront, up to $67.5M contingentBXCL501: under FDA review for at-home useFDA target action date: Nov. 14, 2026Rumi: option to license RTX-7340 (PDE2 inhibitor)RTX-7340: Fragile X; no human data reportedRumi–Enthorin financial terms: not disclosedTeva Acquires BioXcel Neuroscience Assets, Including At-Home Agitation CandidateTeva Pharmaceuticals International GmbH, a subsidiary of Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd., has completed its acquisition of neuroscience assets from BioXcel Therapeutics, Inc., including worldwide rights to BXCL501, an investigational dexmedetomidine sublingual film under FDA review for at-home treatment of agitation in adults with schizophrenia or bipolar I or II disorder.2“Business development plays an important role in accelerating our Pivot to Growth strategy by bringing targeted external innovation into Teva,” says Evan Lippman, executive vice president of business development at Teva. “BXCL501 is a strong strategic fit with our neuroscience portfolio and reflects our disciplined focus on differentiated, late-stage opportunities that address unmet patient needs and create long-term value for Teva’s shareholders.”2Teva paid $57.5 million upfront and could owe up to $67.5 million in contingent payments, some tied to the timing of regulatory approval and others to sales milestones.2 The court-supervised sale proceeded under Section 363 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code and did not include the acquisition of BioXcel itself.2 The assets also include IGALMI (dexmedetomidine), an FDA-approved sublingual film for the same conditions in a hospital setting.2Where does BXCL501 stand with FDA?BioXcel’s quarterly filing states that the supplemental new drug application for at-home use was submitted Jan. 14, 2026, and that FDA set a Nov. 14 target action date, less than three weeks after Teva’s announcement.4 The company reported that the supporting Phase 3 trial was designed to assess safety and was not powered for efficacy, so its efficacy findings are exploratory.4 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void does at-home treatment of agitation matter?Teva, citing its own market research, says acute agitation affects 25% to 40% of patients with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, and that acute treatment options remain limited outside healthcare settings.2“Agitation can escalate quickly, which is why the ability to intervene early matters,” says Eric Hughes, M.D., Ph.D., executive vice president of global research and development and chief medical officer at Teva. “If approved, BXCL501 could give adults living with schizophrenia or bipolar I or II disorder the ability to treat agitation at home, closer to the moment symptoms emerge and before they could become more difficult to manage.”Rumi Therapeutics Enters Option Agreement for Fragile X PDE2 InhibitorRumi Therapeutics, a drug development company within Rumi Scientific Holdings, has entered an option to license agreement with Enthorin Therapeutics for RTX-7340 (ENT-7340), an investigational phosphodiesterase 2 (PDE2) inhibitor for Fragile X syndrome.3 Financial terms were not disclosed. Rumi describes the candidate as ready for an investigational new drug application and says the deal moves it toward clinical development.3Why target PDE2 in Fragile X syndrome?Fragile X syndrome is a genetic neurodevelopmental disorder caused by changes in the FMR1 gene that reduce or eliminate production of a protein important for brain development, and it is a leading inherited cause of intellectual disability.3 The program draws on preclinical Fragile X models, including human organoid studies from sister company Rumi Scientific. Rumi says PDE2A activity is increased in animal models and that inhibiting it has improved dendritic spine maturation, synaptic plasticity, and social and cognitive endpoints.3 An independent 2019 study in Cerebral Cortex found a similar pattern: PDE2A activity was elevated in the brains of Fmr1-knockout mice, and inhibiting it restored dendritic spine maturity and corrected social and communicative deficits in mouse and rat models.5What preclinical data support RTX-7340?Rumi says RTX-7340 studies in Fmr1-knockout mice showed correction of disease-associated electroencephalography abnormalities, which the company plans to use to select neurophysiological measures for clinical evaluation.3“We are pleased to partner with Rumi Therapeutics to advance RTX-7340 toward clinical evaluation in Fragile X syndrome. Rumi Scientific’s human organoid capabilities complement the preclinical development work supporting the candidate and create an opportunity to deepen our understanding of its therapeutic potential. Together, we aim to translate that scientific foundation into a focused clinical development program,” says J. Guy Breitenbucher, PhD, managing partner and co-founder of Enthorin Therapeutics.A clinician quoted in the release addresses the translational question. “A central challenge in Fragile X drug development is connecting a treatment’s effects on disease biology with outcomes that matter to patients. Combining human organoid research with neurophysiological measures creates an opportunity to build that connection more deliberately. A PDE2 program developed around this framework could help us evaluate both whether the drug affects relevant brain function and whether those effects translate into clinical benefit,” says Craig Ericksson, director of the Fragile X Syndrome Research and Treatment Center at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital.What remains unknown about RTX-7340?The evidence cited so far comes from animal models, and the release states that the candidate’s human safety and efficacy have not been established. title: AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 15, 2026 AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff AstraZeneca will pay insitro $40 million upfront to apply AI to target discovery in MASH and cardiomyopathies, with no candidates named yet. Advertisement AstraZeneca has signed a drug discovery collaboration and licensing agreement with insitro to apply artificial intelligence (AI) to target identification and therapeutic design in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies, the companies announced Oct. 15.1,2 Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in milestones.1,2Sharon Barr, executive vice president and head of BioPharmaceuticals research and development at AstraZeneca, tied the agreement to target selection: “We know that disease biology is incredibly complex, and one of the most critical decisions in R&D is selecting the right target. This strategic collaboration underscores our commitment to maximizing the potential of cutting-edge AI to tackle the root cause of disease. Partnering with insitro, we will use advanced AI to identify the biological drivers of disease to support the rapid discovery of high-quality novel targets, advancing our ambition to deliver the next generation of medicines to patients faster.”1“MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights.”What are AstraZeneca and insitro agreeing to do?Insitro will use its Virtual Human platform to identify causal disease biology in both indications and advance AstraZeneca-nominated targets from discovery to development candidate.1,2 The platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design.1AstraZeneca will take the clinical development and regulatory work and holds exclusive worldwide rights to the selected programs; insitro’s release adds that AstraZeneca will also lead commercialization.1,2Beyond the upfront payment, insitro is eligible for single-digit royalties on global sales.1,2 The two releases describe the milestones slightly differently: AstraZeneca cites development and commercial milestones, while insitro includes discovery milestones.1,2The upfront payment represents less than 3% of the combined headline value, and neither company disclosed the number of targets, program timelines or payment schedule.Why are MASH and cardiomyopathies difficult to treat?Insitro’s release says each disease is defined by heterogeneity, with a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs, which has complicated treatment.2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); Daphne Koller, Ph.D., founder and CEO of insitro, said: “MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights. Our platform simultaneously deconvolutes disease biology and identifies causal drivers of disease pathologies. Partnering with AstraZeneca allows us to pair our deep biological precision with their pharmaceutical expertise and scale with potential for accelerated advancement of novel programs through development and to patients.”2In MASH, the treatment landscape has changed recently. The FDA approved resmetirom (Rezdiffra) in March 2024 under its accelerated approval pathway for adults with noncirrhotic disease and moderate to advanced liver scarring, to be used with diet and exercise. The agency, which at the time referred to the condition as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, said patients had previously lacked a medication that directly addressed their liver damage, and cited an estimate of 6 million to 8 million U.S. patients at that disease stage.3The cardiomyopathy picture is less defined in the releases, which do not specify which forms are in scope. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the most common inherited cardiovascular disorder, is estimated to affect 1 in 500 people, and a published review notes that existing studies may have underestimated its prevalence.4 That offers one illustration of the underdiagnosis Koller describes, though it should not be read as the collaboration’s target population.How does the collaboration fit each company’s portfolio?AstraZeneca describes cardiovascular, renal and metabolism as one of its main disease areas and a key growth driver, with an emphasis on the links among the heart, kidneys, liver and pancreas.1 A program spanning a liver disease and heart muscle diseases fits within that framing.Insitro says it has built a multimodal corpus of human and cellular data since 2018 and is advancing nine programs, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.2 The company reports more than $750 million in capital and existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead.2 The release does not say how its internal liver programs relate to targets AstraZeneca will nominate.What remains unknown about the collaboration?No candidate, efficacy data or safety data accompany the announcement, and the collaboration sits at the discovery stage. Targets identified through AI-driven analysis of human data will still need validation through preclinical work and clinical trials, where heterogeneity of disease could also affect trial design. Milestone and royalty figures are potential payments contingent on progress that neither company has timed publicly. Neither release addresses market reaction, and independent verification of the platform’s performance in these indications was not available at the time of publication.SourcesAstraZeneca announces new strategic collaboration with insitro to use advanced AI systems to develop transformative therapeutics for difficult to treat cardiometabolic diseases. MADRID — A personalized mRNA cancer vaccine reduced the risk of disease recurrence in patients with melanoma by 42% compared to a standard treatment, according to a large clinical trial conducted by the drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The results are an important advance for the treatment of melanoma, oncologists said, because patients lived significantly longer without their cancer returning. Advertisement The success of the Moderna-Merck vaccine, intismeran autogene, may also usher in a new wave of treatments for other types of cancer, though experts are debating how broadly applicable the technology could be. The medicine is an individualized therapy that attacks the unique mutations, called neoantigens, found in a patient’s tumor. MADRID — The combination of an experimental drug from Tango Therapeutics and Revolution Medicines’ Rasonque led to tumor responses in 82% of patients with a certain type of advanced pancreatic cancer, clinical trial results reported Friday showed. The responses were also durable: 88% of the patients were still alive without tumor progression when assessed at nine months. A rare disease drug previously rejected by the Food and Drug Administration will get a second look, giving its developer, Biohaven, another shot at a regulatory clearance. This Biohaven “2.0” is led by the same management team as the original, but has been pursuing a pipeline of medicines for multiple different diseases. The most advanced of those therapies is Vyglxia. Biohaven has been developing it for a group of rare genetic disorders collectively called spinocerebellar ataxia, through which progressive neuronal damage leads to problems with balance, coordination and speech. If approved, it could be the first marketed medicine for the condition. Some analysts have predicted north of $1 billion in annual sales. Yet Vyglxia has encountered roadblocks with multiple drug regulators. In Europe, the company withdrew an approval application after evaluators there questioned Biohaven’s supportive evidence. U.S. regulators were similarly skeptical. Despite findings suggesting Vyglxia might slow disease progression by as much as 70%, the FDA found the key experiment the company ran unconvincing in part because of its design. The regulator formally rejected the treatment last November. Biohaven claimed to have been blindsided by the decision, which was one of many controversial rare disease drug rejections issued by former FDA leadership. It also turned to cost cuts afterwards. It’s also expressed a desire to become more flexible in reviewing rare disease medicines, specifically. That shift in stance “opens a real possibility” that Vyglxia could get to market, added RBC Capital Markets analyst Leonid Timashev. We appreciate feedback, criticism, and tips. … Amid ongoing angst over prescription drug prices, the median net price for 202 newly launched medicines, when adjusted for inflation and manufacturer discounts, rose by 35% to $257,000 in 2025 from $190,000 in 2022, STAT writes, citing an analysis by the Institute for Clinical and Economic Review and West Health. About one in four drugs launched in 2025 had an annual net price exceeding $500,000, while another 34% were priced between $200,000 and $500,000. At the same time, though, the most substantial increase in net launch prices occurred between 2022 and 2023; last year, there was a 2% decline.Advertisement Novo Nordisk disclosed that its next-generation experimental drug, CagriSema, showed 25% weight loss on average in women with obesity or overweight in a late-stage study, according to Reuters. CagriSema, viewed ‌as a successor to its big-selling weight loss drug Wegovy, could help Novo claw back ground lost to Eli Lilly in the weight loss market. Wegovy faces ​patent expirations after 2030. Novo said a 2.4-milligram dose of CagriSema ​was associated with an average weight loss of 25% after ⁠68 weeks in 2,309 women, ​compared with 3% weight loss in women on placebo. In the full trial ​of more than 3,400 adults, CagriSema led to 22.7% weight loss, below the 25% Novo had targeted. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account? title: FDA Extends Talzenna-Xtandi to Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 26, 2026 FDA Extends Talzenna-Xtandi to Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff Pfizer’s talazoparib-enzalutamide combination moves to earlier line in prostate cancer, with eligibility tied to genetic testing and immature survival data. Advertisement The FDA today expanded the approval of Talzenna (talazoparib) plus Xtandi (enzalutamide) to men with metastatic prostate cancer that has not been treated with androgen pathway drugs, or remains sensitive to them, and that carries homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene mutations, according to Pfizer.1 The regimen, first cleared in 2023 for castration-resistant disease, now reaches an earlier stage of treatment, with eligibility depending on a positive biomarker test.2 For Pfizer, the decision moves a combination the company describes as an established standard-of-care option into an earlier line of therapy, where it says more patients may experience benefit. Aamir Malik, executive vice president and chief U.S. commercial officer at Pfizer, said in the announcement: “Today’s approval of Talzenna plus Xtandi builds on its established role as a standard-of-care option for men with advanced prostate cancer. Moving this targeted therapy into the androgen pathway modulation-naïve or -sensitive setting further reflects our commitment to men with HRR-mutated metastatic prostate cancer, providing a new option at a stage where it may have a greater impact to delay progression.”1Key FactsDrug: talazoparib (PARP inhibitor) + enzalutamideIndication: HRR-mutated metastatic prostate cancerTrial: Phase 3 TALAPRO-3, 599 patientsEfficacy: 52% lower risk of progression or deathSafety: Grade 3 or higher anemia, 51% vs. 3%Status: FDA-approved Oct. 26, 2026 (U.S.)Europe: European Medicines Agency review ongoingWhat indication did the FDA approve, and who qualifies?The label covers adults whose tumors carry HRR mutations detected by an FDA-authorized test, spanning 12 genes rather than BRCA1 and BRCA2 alone.2 Two previously approved FoundationOne assays, one using tumor tissue and one using a liquid biopsy, can identify eligible patients.2 The recommended Talzenna dose is 0.5 mg orally once daily with Xtandi until progression or unacceptable toxicity, alongside androgen deprivation therapy.2 The agency granted priority review and conducted the assessment under Project Orbis, a framework for concurrent oncology reviews with international regulators.2What did the TALAPRO-3 trial show?TALAPRO-3 randomized 599 patients with HRR-mutated disease to Talzenna 0.5 mg or placebo daily, each combined with Xtandi 160 mg.1 The primary endpoint was investigator-assessed radiographic progression-free survival.1 Talzenna plus Xtandi reduced the risk of radiographic progression or death by 52% (hazard ratio, 0.48; Pfizer estimates that 77% of patients remained progression-free at three years.1 The results were published in The New England Journal of Medicine.3Pfizer reported no new safety signals. The most common grade 3 or higher adverse event was anemia, affecting 51% of the talazoparib group and 3% of controls, and 5% of patients stopped talazoparib because of anemia.1Why does earlier treatment matter in HRR-mutated prostate cancer?Pfizer says about 25% of patients with hormone-sensitive metastatic prostate cancer have HRR mutations.1 Neeraj Agarwal, M.D., global lead investigator for TALAPRO-3, said: “This approval represents a critical advancement for patients with newly diagnosed metastatic prostate cancer with HRR gene mutations, who face a more aggressive disease, worse prognosis, and limited treatment options. In the TALAPRO-3 trial, clinical benefits were consistent for patients with BRCA and non-BRCA HRR gene mutations, addressing a long-standing unmet need – and reinforcing the importance of biomarker testing at the time of diagnosis.”1Because eligibility requires a positive test, the number of patients who receive the regimen will depend partly on how consistently genotyping occurs at diagnosis.How does the approval fit the drug’s regulatory history?Talzenna was first approved as a single agent for certain germline BRCA-mutated breast cancers. The FDA cleared the combination in June 2023 for HRR-mutated castration-resistant prostate cancer, and the European Commission followed in January 2024 for castration-resistant disease in patients for whom chemotherapy is not clinically indicated.1 Pfizer says the combination is approved in more than 60 countries, with indications varying by country.1 The castration-resistant approval rested on TALAPRO-2, in which unselected patients had a hazard ratio of 0.63 for progression or death with Talzenna plus Xtandi versus placebo plus enzalutamide.4What limitations and open questions remain?Overall survival data were immature at the time of the analysis, and the FDA announcement did not report survival estimates.2 Pfizer’s own risk disclosures list whether TALAPRO-3 will meet its key secondary overall survival endpoint as an uncertainty.1 Because the Talzenna arm has not reached median radiographic progression-free survival, the absolute difference between arms is not yet defined, and the 45.8-month control median indicates that Xtandi alone also provides prolonged disease control in this population.2 The primary endpoint also relied on investigator assessment, which can differ from blinded independent review.1Prescribing information carries warnings for myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia, with a cumulative incidence of about 1% across talazoparib studies, as well as myelosuppression requiring monthly blood count monitoring and embryo-fetal toxicity.1 The European Medicines Agency is reviewing the same indication.1SourcesPfizer’s Talzenna plus Xtandi FDA-approved for an earlier metastatic prostate cancer treatment setting. title: 康方生物依沃西单抗胆道癌新适应症拟纳入优先审评，全球首创PD-1/VEGF双抗再拓实体瘤版图

关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 昨天 11:16 1910 PD-1 VEGF 中山康方生物医药有限公司 依沃西单抗 胆道癌 10月23日，CDE官网公示，康方生物的依沃西单抗注射液一项新适应症拟纳入优先审评，拟用于联合化疗一线治疗局部晚期或转移性胆道癌。图源：CDE官网此次申报进展与Ⅲ期临床研究HARMONi-GI1取得积极结果有关。2026年8月，康方生物宣布，该研究在预设期中分析中达到总生存期（OS）主要终点，并达到无进展生存期（PFS）和客观缓解率（ORR）的全部关键次要终点。一、胆道癌Ⅲ期研究取得阳性结果依沃西单抗是康方生物自主研发的PD-1/VEGF双特异性抗体，也是全球首创的PD-1/VEGF双特异性肿瘤免疫治疗药物。摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库显示，2024年该品种在中国首次上市。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库本次拟纳入优先审评的新适应症为依沃西单抗联合化疗一线治疗局部晚期或转移性胆道癌。在Ⅲ期临床研究AK112-309/HARMONi-GI1中，研究人员采用随机、双盲、对照、多中心设计，评估依沃西单抗联合化疗与度伐利尤单抗联合化疗一线治疗晚期胆道恶性肿瘤的疗效与安全性。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库2026年8月，康方生物宣布，经独立数据监察委员会（IDMC）评估的预设期中分析显示，HARMONi-GI1研究达到OS主要终点，结果具有统计学显著性；同时达到PFS和ORR的全部关键次要终点。康方生物在新闻稿中表示，度伐利尤单抗联合化疗是国内外指南共同推荐的一线标准治疗方案（SOC）。公司称，HARMONi-GI1是胆道癌领域首个以PD-L1单抗联合化疗为对照、取得OS显著阳性结果的Ⅲ期研究。该研究结果已入选2026年欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）大会突破性摘要（LBA8，主席论坛），康方生物将于大会首次披露具体研究数据。二、依沃西单抗持续拓展适应症目前，依沃西单抗已在中国获批三项适应症，覆盖EGFR-TKI耐药的非鳞状非小细胞肺癌（nsq-NSCLC）、PD-L1阳性非小细胞肺癌一线治疗及鳞状非小细胞肺癌一线治疗。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库除国内市场外，依沃西单抗也在推进海外商业化。2022年12月，康方生物将依沃西单抗部分海外权益授权给美国Summit Therapeutics，交易方案包括50亿美元以上的潜在付款及两位数百分比的销售提成。目前，依沃西单抗联合化疗用于第三代EGFR-TKI治疗后进展的EGFR突变非鳞状非小细胞肺癌的美国上市申请正在审评中。此次胆道癌新适应症拟纳入优先审评，意味着依沃西单抗在肺癌之外进一步拓展实体瘤治疗领域。后续研究具体数据及审评进展，值得持续关注。参考来源：[1] CDE官网[2] Bristol Myers Squibb on Friday reported that one patient died after receiving its investigational CAR-T therapy in an early autoimmune trial, adding to safety concerns about a growing field of research. In a Phase 1 trial that tested the therapy in multiple sclerosis, a condition that causes muscle weakness and extreme fatigue, the patient experienced motor symptoms that did not resolve with standard autoimmune treatments. title: 罗氏divarasib头对头Ⅲ期临床研究数据出炉，KRAS G12C突变NSCLC患者死亡风险直降44%
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 罗氏divarasib头对头Ⅲ期临床研究数据出炉，KRAS G12C突变NSCLC患者死亡风险直降44% 罗氏divarasib头对头Ⅲ期临床研究数据出炉，KRAS G12C突变NSCLC患者死亡风险直降44% 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 19小时前 1103 罗氏 KRAS G12C抑制剂 divarasib 临床研究 NSCLC 10月25日，在欧洲临床肿瘤学会（ESMO）大会上，罗氏公布了下一代KRAS G12C抑制剂divarasib的Ⅲ期临床研究Krascendo 1最新数据。结果显示，在既往接受过治疗的KRAS G12C突变非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）患者中，与对照组已获批的KRAS G12C抑制剂相比，divarasib将患者死亡风险降低44%，无进展生存期（PFS）和客观缓解率（ORR）也均取得改善。图源：罗氏官网此次研究直接比较了divarasib与安进的Lumakras（sotorasib）、百时美施贵宝（BMS）的Krazati（adagrasib），为其在KRAS G12C突变NSCLC领域的竞争力提供了进一步证据。一、死亡风险降低44%，OS、PFS双双改善Krascendo 1是一项纳入338例患者的Ⅲ期临床研究，旨在评估divarasib在既往接受过治疗的KRAS G12C突变NSCLC患者中的疗效与安全性。今年7月，罗氏首次公布该研究的顶线结果，宣布divarasib在总生存期（OS）和无进展生存期（PFS）方面，较Lumakras和Krazati取得具有临床意义和统计学显著性的改善，但当时尚未披露具体数据。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库10月25日公布的最新分析进一步揭示了这一优势。在生存获益方面，divarasib组中位OS达到17.7个月，对照组为12.0个月，死亡风险降低44%（HR=0.56）。在疾病进展方面，divarasib组中位PFS达到9.8个月，对照组为5.7个月，疾病进展或死亡风险降低42%。在肿瘤缓解方面，divarasib组确认的客观缓解率（ORR）达到58%，对照组为32%。从中位OS、PFS到ORR，divarasib均显示出疗效优势。其中，OS结果尤其受到关注，意味着该药的临床获益不仅体现在延缓疾病进展，也体现在患者生存结局的改善。罗氏首席医学官Levi Garraway表示，这项头对头研究的结果凸显了divarasib为既往接受过治疗的KRAS G12C突变肺癌患者带来新治疗选择的潜力，并进一步支持其同类最佳（best-in-class）的定位。二、疗效之外，安全性数据同步披露除疗效结果外，此次公布的数据还进一步呈现了divarasib的安全性特征。研究显示，divarasib的安全性特征与KRAS G12C抑制剂已知的类效应基本一致，最常见的治疗相关不良事件（TRAE）包括胃肠道毒性和肝毒性。其中，胃肠道不良事件主要表现为腹泻、恶心和呕吐。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库值得关注的是，divarasib组严重腹泻发生率为9%，高于对照组的3%；但因治疗相关不良事件而中断治疗的发生率仅为4.8%，低于对照组的11.7%。此外，研究显示，divarasib在OS和PFS方面的临床获益在各临床相关亚组中保持一致，且不受PD-L1表达水平或KEAP1突变状态影响。整体来看，divarasib在展现疗效优势的同时，也呈现出值得进一步关注的安全性数据。不过，严重腹泻发生率较高这一信号仍需结合更完整的安全性数据进行评估。三、一线治疗布局同步推进除针对既往接受过治疗患者的Krascendo 1研究外，罗氏还在推进divarasib的一线治疗布局。Ⅲ期Krascendo 2研究旨在评估divarasib联合默沙东Keytruda（pembrolizumab）的无化疗方案，对比化疗联合免疫治疗，用于KRAS G12C突变NSCLC一线治疗的疗效与安全性。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库如果后续研究取得积极结果，divarasib有望进一步拓展其在KRAS G12C突变NSCLC治疗中的应用空间。从目前公布的Ⅲ期数据来看，divarasib已在既往接受过治疗的患者中展现出OS、PFS及ORR方面的优势。随着一线治疗研究推进，其后续临床进展值得持续关注。参考来源：[1] 企业官网/官方披露[2] 摩熵医药（原药融云）数据库扩展阅读：1. 罗氏11.6亿美元重金引进大睿生物ALK7 RNAi，同步押注非GLP-1减重与RAS G12V肿瘤双赛道2. title: Bristol Myers Squibb Discloses Patient Death in CAR-T Multiple Sclerosis Trial
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 26, 2026 Bristol Myers Squibb Discloses Patient Death in CAR-T Multiple Sclerosis Trial Author(s)Nicholas Jacobus Bristol Myers Squibb discloses results from it's Phase I Breakfree-2 trial of CAR-T therapy zola-cel for multiple sclerosis. Advertisement Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) has disclosed a patient death in its early-stage Breakfree-2 trial studying zolacabtagene autoleucel, an investigational, autologous CD19-directed CAR T cell therapy, in patients with relapsing or progressive forms of multiple sclerosis (MS).The death was disclosed as part of a broader data readout presented in an oral presentation at MSToronto 2026 and follows the company’s decision to place a voluntary pause on zola-cel studies back in September.What happened to the patient?The patient, who had highly active relapsing MS, died of septic pneumonia one day after receiving high-dose chemotherapy and 44 days after zola-cel infusion.1 According to BMS, the patient experienced late-onset, non-ICANS motor symptoms following infusion that did not resolve with intermittent corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin.Although the patient’s CAR-T cell expansion was consistent with that observed across the study, physicians administered high-dose cyclophosphamide, after which the patient developed septic pneumonia and died the following day. A BMS spokesperson told Reuters, “The patient had a late onset side effect, a series of other complications and was heavily pretreated prior to CAR T, confounding our ability to determine the root cause of the issue.”2 BMS says the death was unrelated to the earlier voluntary pause and that no additional Grade 5 events have occurred across any zola-cel autoimmune disease program, which has treated 190 patients in Phase I studies to date. Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome occurred in 7.6% of patients (5 of 66), mostly Grade 1 or 2 and resolving in a median of two days; one Grade 4 case occurred in a progressive MS patient and resolved within four days after treatment with corticosteroids and anakinra.1 BMS says the majority of adverse events were brief and reversible, consistent with previously reported zola-cel data.On efficacy, all patients treated at dose level 2 (60 of 60) remained off disease-modifying therapies at last follow-up, including nine patients followed for more than 12 months.1 Among evaluable patients at dose level 2 with at least 26 weeks of follow-up, six of seven relapsing MS patients met criteria for no evidence of disease activity, and 22 of 24 progressive MS patients showed stability or improvement in disability progression despite prior worsening at baseline.BMS frames the data as supportive of zola-cel’s broader potential despite the fatality. “BMS is at the forefront of cell therapy science, pioneering a new era by exploring the potential for immune reset in patients living with autoimmune diseases,” says Lynelle B. Hoch, president of the Cell Therapy Organization at Bristol Myers Squibb. “The Breakfree-2 data demonstrate clinical potential for zola-cel in multiple sclerosis, showcasing the opportunity for treatment-free remission in patients who have depended on chronic therapies for years.”Jeffrey A. Cohen, professor of neurology and staff physician at the Cleveland Clinic’s Mellen Center, offers a more measured outside assessment. “These data suggest that CD19-directed CAR-T cell therapy may offer a new approach to treating multiple sclerosis,” he says. “While more research is needed, the potential to control relapses, stabilize disability and reduce reliance on disease-modifying medications is encouraging.”What’s next?With BMS now coordinating directly with the FDA on a restart timeline targeting early 2027, the company’s ability to resolve outstanding safety questions will likely determine how quickly, and how broadly, zola-cel can advance toward later-stage development in MS and other autoimmune diseases.SourcesBristol Myers Squibb Presents Results from Phase 1 Breakfree-2 Study of Zolacabtagene Autoleucel (BMS-986353) in Patients with Highly Active Relapsing and Progressive Forms of Multiple Sclerosis at MSToronto 2026 Bristol Myers Squibb October 23, 2026, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261022949204/en/Bristol-Myers-Squibb-Presents-Results-from-Phase-1-Breakfree-2-Study-of-Zolacabtagene-Autoleucel-BMS-986353-in-Patients-with-Highly-Active-Relapsing-and-Progressive-Forms-of-Multiple-Sclerosis-at-MSToronto-2026Bristol Myers discloses patient death in early-stage cell therapy study Reuters October 23, 2026, https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/bristol-myers-discloses-patient-death-early-stage-cell-therapy-study-2026-10-23/ Newsletter Lead with insight with the Pharmaceutical Executive newsletter, featuring strategic analysis, leadership trends, and market intelligence for biopharma decision-makers. title: Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 19, 2026 Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More Foundayo’s EU backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s masked TCE deal, FDA’s rare disease reset, and Bausch + Lomb’s new interim CEO — explained. Advertisement Lilly’s Foundayo Receives Positive CHMP Opinion for EuropeWhat did the EMA committee recommend?The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended granting marketing authorization in the EU for Foundayo (orforglipron) for two indications: weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, and the treatment of type 2 diabetes in adults whose blood glucose is not adequately controlled. The European Commission makes the final approval decision and typically follows CHMP recommendations within a few weeks.What is Foundayo and why does it matter?Foundayo is Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 receptor agonist — a once-daily pill that can be taken at any time of day without food and water restrictions. That last point distinguishes it from other oral GLP-1 therapies currently on the market. The drug received FDA approval for obesity in April 2026 and launched commercially in the United States in the second quarter. Lilly has submitted orforglipron for regulatory review in approximately 40 markets globally.The Stories Covered in this PieceEMA Panel Backs Lilly’s Foundayo for Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes in EuropeFDA Approves Enspryng (Satralizumab) for Thyroid Eye DiseaseAstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 BillionFDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeVir Biotechnology Enters R&D Collaboration with Gilead for Three Novel PRO-XTEN Dual Masked T-Cell EngagersBausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat does this mean competitively?If the European Commission approves Foundayo, it would become the second oral GLP-1 available in the EU for weight management, following Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill, which received European approval in July for weight management only. In the type 2 diabetes setting, Foundayo would compete with Novo’s Rybelsus brand of oral semaglutide, which has been on the European market since 2020 and has grown into a multi-billion-dollar franchise. The CHMP recommendation opens a new competitive front between Lilly and Novo Nordisk in Europe’s oral GLP-1 market, adding to their existing rivalry in injectable incretin therapies.What did the clinical evidence show?The weight management recommendation is based on two studies involving more than 4,740 adults with obesity or overweight. The type 2 diabetes recommendation is based on four studies involving 3,765 adults compared against placebo, dapagliflozin, and oral semaglutide.FDA Approves Enspryng for Thyroid Eye DiseaseWhat was approved?The FDA approved Enspryng (satralizumab), an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor developed by Roche, for adults with thyroid eye disease on October 16. Roche describes it as the first subcutaneous therapy for the condition — one that patients or caregivers can administer at home after training from a healthcare provider. It is Enspryng’s second indication; the drug was first approved in 2020 for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.What did the clinical trials show?The approval rests on two identically designed Phase 3 trials, SatraGO-1 and SatraGO-2, which enrolled 258 adults across 19 countries. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with active, moderate-to-severe disease who achieved at least a 2 mm reduction in proptosis — eye bulging — at week 24. Results diverged: SatraGO-2 met its endpoint, with 52.9% of Enspryng-treated patients achieving a proptosis response versus 23.4% on placebo, and 60.7% showing reduced double vision versus 25.8%. SatraGO-1 did not reach statistical significance, with researchers attributing the gap to an unexpectedly high placebo response.How does this change the treatment landscape?Two disease-specific therapies were already approved — Tepezza and, more recently, Lumvoa — both administered by intravenous infusion. Enspryng’s subcutaneous, every-four-week maintenance dosing offers a different treatment experience, with the key benefit being reduced logistical burden rather than a demonstrated efficacy advantage over existing options. No head-to-head comparison with approved therapies was conducted.What are the remaining unknowns?Roche did not disclose pricing or launch timing. Long-term data beyond week 24 were not described in available sources. Separately, the FDA has granted priority review to a supplemental Enspryng application for myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, with a decision expected in January 2027. Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in development and commercial milestones, plus single-digit royalties on global sales.What is insitro’s platform?Insitro’s Virtual Human platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design. The company was founded in 2018 and reports more than $750 million in capital raised, with existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead. It has nine programs in development, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.Why MASH and cardiomyopathies?Both conditions are characterized by disease heterogeneity — a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs — which has complicated treatment development. In MASH, the FDA approved its first treatment, resmetirom (Rezdiffra), in March 2024, but the condition still lacks therapeutic options for most of the estimated 6 to 8 million US patients with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring. The cardiomyopathy scope was not specified in the announcement.What are the limitations of this deal?No drug candidates were named in the announcement. The collaboration sits at the discovery stage, with targets identified through AI-driven analysis still requiring validation through preclinical and clinical work. The $40 million upfront represents less than 3% of the total headline value, and neither company disclosed timelines for milestone payments.FDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeWhat is the Rare Disease Framework Initiative?The FDA announced a new effort to redesign how drugs and biologics for rare diseases are developed and reviewed. The initiative, outlined in a white paper released by the agency’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, aims to build a regulatory framework tailored to the realities of small patient populations — covering clinical development, evidence standards, manufacturing review, and the role of patient voice throughout the process.Why is FDA doing this now?Despite years of regulatory flexibility programs for rare diseases, only approximately 5% of rare conditions currently have an FDA-approved treatment. The agency says that gap reflects the need for a more fundamentally tailored approach rather than incremental adjustments to a framework originally designed for common diseases.What are the specific commitments?The initiative outlines six priority areas: greater clarity and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance; embedding the patient voice early and at defined milestones; leveraging external expertise for customized review; building shared institutional knowledge; applying risk-based approaches to manufacturing and pre-approval inspections; and championing innovative statistical approaches in rare disease development.What happens next?The FDA is hosting a public meeting on October 28 at its White Oak campus, facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation, to gather input from patients, disease advocates, industry, and other stakeholders. Additional sector-specific roundtables and requests for information will follow. The detailed framework development — which could include new guidance, regulatory changes, and organizational changes within FDA — will be informed by that input.Gilead and Vir Biotechnology Enter $1.87 Billion Masked T-Cell Engager CollaborationWhat are the two companies agreeing to develop?Vir Biotechnology will discover and optimize three novel PRO-XTEN dual-masked T-cell engager development candidates for Gilead, targeting selected solid tumor-associated antigens. Gilead holds an exclusive license to develop, manufacture and commercialize the resulting therapies. Vir will receive $90 million upfront — including $65 million in cash and a $25 million equity investment at a 30% premium — and is eligible for up to $1.74 billion in additional milestones and tiered royalties.What is the PRO-XTEN masking technology?PRO-XTEN is designed to keep T-cell engagers inactive in circulation until they reach the tumor microenvironment, where tumor-specific proteases cleave the mask and activate the drug’s cancer-killing mechanism. That conditional activation is intended to limit systemic toxicity — one of the primary barriers to TCE use in solid tumors — while extending the drug’s half-life and potentially enabling less frequent dosing.Why does this matter for solid tumor oncology?T-cell engagers have proven highly effective in blood cancers but have faced significant limitations in solid tumors, where toxicity and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment have constrained clinical use. Vir’s PRO-XTEN approach directly targets those barriers. This is the second major PRO-XTEN collaboration — an earlier $1.7 billion deal with Astellas for a PSMA-targeted TCE in prostate cancer was announced in February 2026. Together the two deals bring total PRO-XTEN platform value to more than $3.6 billion across two top-tier pharma partners.How does this fit Gilead’s oncology strategy?Today’s deal is Gilead’s third major solid tumor oncology transaction in 2026, following the $5 billion Tubulis ADC acquisition in April and the $2.1 billion Ouro Medicines BCMA T-cell engager acquisition in March. Gilead is simultaneously building in ADCs, T-cell engagers for autoimmune disease, and now masked T-cell engagers for solid tumors — a deliberate multi-mechanism oncology buildout executed across a single year.Bausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat happened at Bausch + Lomb?Bausch + Lomb announced that Brent Saunders departed as CEO by mutual agreement, with Thomas J. Appio named interim CEO effective immediately. Appio, who will retain his role as CEO of parent company Bausch Health, steps into the position just weeks before the company reports third-quarter results and updates its full-year guidance on October 28.What does the company expect for 2026?Simultaneously with the leadership announcement, both Bausch + Lomb and Bausch Health said they expect to raise their full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance based on preliminary third-quarter results, citing strong business performance and anticipated momentum through year-end.What was Saunders building?Saunders returned to Bausch + Lomb in March 2023 — his second stint as CEO — and spent three years stabilizing the company’s supply chain, accelerating commercial execution, and rebuilding its R&D pipeline. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to another working week. We hope the weekend respite was relaxing and invigorating because that oh-too-familiar routine of meetings, deadlines, and the like has returned with a vengeance. But what can you do? The world, such as it is, continues to rotate. To nudge it in a better direction, we are brewing another cup of stimulation. Our choice today is butter pecan with a dash of raw honey. Feel free to join us. Remember, no prescription is required. Meanwhile, here are some tidbits to help you along. Best of luck accomplishing your goals today, and of course, do keep in touch. … Bristol Myers Squibb reported that one patient died after receiving its investigational CAR-T therapy in an early autoimmune trial, adding to safety concerns about a growing field of research, STAT notes. In a Phase 1 trial that tested the therapy in multiple sclerosis, the patient experienced motor symptoms that did not resolve with standard autoimmune treatments. They were then given a potent immunosuppressant, but developed septic pneumonia and died, Bristol said in a press release. In a subsequent statement, Bristol said this patient was treated for a series of other complications prior to receiving the CAR-T therapy, “confounding our ability to determine the root cause of the issue.”Advertisement A Roche drug billed as a potential blockbuster helped patients with a form of lung cancer that had spread live almost six months longer than two competitive medicines, Bloomberg News says. The experimental treatment, called divarasib, fared better than similar drugs from Amgen and Bristol Myers Squibb in a late-stage study. The drug was given to patients with non-small cell lung cancer that had spread, in part because of a genetic mutation, after other treatments, including chemotherapy. The findings could help divarasib become the treatment of choice for this type of lung cancer, in which a mutation called KRAS G12C drives the tumor cell growth. 近日（10月22日），NMPA官网显示，齐鲁制药申报的4类仿制药泊那替尼片获批生产。摩熵医药数据库显示，此前该品种在国内仅原研药及成都硕德药业拥有生产批文。此次齐鲁制药获批，成为国内第2家获批该品种的药企。图源：NMPA官网泊那替尼片由武田/大冢制药开发，是一款第三代BCR-ABL激酶抑制剂，可抑制BCR-ABL及其T315I突变，适用于慢性髓系白血病、急性淋巴细胞白血病等相关患者。该药曾被纳入第一批临床急需境外新药名单，原研药于2024年9月获批进入中国市场，目前尚未纳入国家医保目录。从市场表现来看，摩熵医药数据库显示泊那替尼2025年全球销售额超过1.3亿美元。 content: 首页 资讯 摩熵视野 交易并购 Walmart与General Medicine合作升级Better Care Services打造综合医疗市场【AI生成】 Walmart与General Medicine合作升级Better Care Services打造综合医疗市场【AI生成】 Fierce 昨天 20:00 查看原文 168 Walmart Inc 沃尔玛（Walmart）宣布与初创公司General Medicine达成合作，旨在将其数字健康平台“Better Care Services”升级为更全面的医疗服务市场。该更新版服务今日正式上线，依托General Medicine的“医疗商店”基础设施，将原有的单一提供商目录扩展为包含超过900种产品和服务的综合平台，涵盖虚拟及线下急诊护理、实验室检测以及针对初级保健、慢性病、心理健康等领域的远程医疗服务。新平台整合了General Michael Santiago/Getty Images via Getty Images Dive Brief: Corxel Pharmaceuticals, a drug startup developing a pair of weight loss medicines, announced Monday plans to go public by merging with a special purpose acquisition company. The SPAC deal and concurrent $300 million private investment will help Corxel take CX11, a GLP-1 pill licensed from the Chinese drug developer Vincentage Pharma, into late-stage testing. In June, Corxel said CX11 helped participants in a U.S. Phase 2 trial lose an average of up to 11.5% of their body weight after 36 weeks while displaying a “favorable” gastrointestinal tolerability profile. The combined company will also advance a preclinical weight loss prospect directed at a different gut hormone known as amylin. A third drug licensed from Biogen and in development for acute ischemic stroke isn't part of the deal and will instead be housed in a parent entity. What followed was a split, with two obesity drugs being merged into a publicly traded entity and the rest of Corxel funneled into a still-private parent. “Both companies have separate development strategies and financing processes, so that’s more welcome news to the investors,” Xie said. Formerly known as Ji Xing Pharmaceuticals, Corxel launched in 2019 and once planned to develop a nasal spray for dry eye disease. It offloaded that therapy in 2024, the same year it acquired from Biogen most rights to JX10 and licensed CX11 from Vincentage. CX11 was already in human testing when Corxel struck that deal. Now it’s on the verge of a global late-stage study. Corxel reported positive late-stage data in May from a Chinese trial run by Vincentage. An international Phase 3 test could follow as soon as the first quarter of 2027. Corxel is pitching CX11 as a “differentiated, next-generation” therapy and an option for people who don’t stay on injectable GLP-1s. Though it is well behind first-to-market oral GLP-1s like Eli Lilly’s Foundayo and Novo’s Wegovy pill, Xie said CX11 may be appealing to people who need to lose 5% to 10% of their body weight and are classified as overweight, but not obese. (Around 31% of U.S. adults fit this description, according to one National Institutes of Health estimate.) Corxel is testing higher doses of CX11 in a Phase 1b trial in an effort to explore the drug’s “efficacy upside,” according to a statement. Additional data are expected in the first half of 2027.
